body: Can u provide reproduction in plunkr?

Here is the plunkr
https://plnkr.co/edit/YTdbKDYP3UbQmQ9wODpM?p=preview
show browser's debug console, type `1` into first input field.
Any updates on this? As said above, this causes all valueChanges subscriptions within the disabled form group to emit an event.
I can confirm I am also seeing this issue.

confirm also, this is currently causing a breaking change on our application due to a valueChanges feedback loop
(commenting to follow this)

Just spent a lot of hours figuring out why valueChanges was triggered on my FormControl, when I changed the disable/enable status of my Form.

Here's another Plunker using latest Angular version
https://plnkr.co/edit/RgyDItYtEfzlLVB6P5f3?p=preview

Created this q on SO
http://stackoverflow.com/questions/43541897/valuechanges-on-formcontrol-triggers-when-form-enable-even-with-emitevent-fals
+1. Any word on this?
Also seeing this issue. We are wanting to use Reactive forms in our large application that has complex and nested forms and I consider this a blocking bug.
I also encountered this bug when I tried to disable field during async validation process, it triggered an endless flow of valueChanges / disable-enable events.
I also have the same error, please we need a response.

I'm also seeing an issue where enabling/disabling a nested form group with emitEvent = false, enables/disables all of the children without passing emitEvent to the children. 

In my application, the child controls of that nested form group are subscribing to valueChanges of their sibling controls. So when the parent form group is enabled, there is an event emitted for each child control. This is breaking the enable/disable logic I have, because we don't want the form group's child controls to update/enable/disable, just because I enabled their form group.

I will create a separate issue for this with details and plunker.

I wonder why emitEvent is not passed to the children here [in disable()](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/c59c390cdcd825cca67a422bc8738f7cd9ad42c5/packages/forms/src/model.ts#L318) and here [in enable()](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/c59c390cdcd825cca67a422bc8738f7cd9ad42c5/packages/forms/src/model.ts#L339)

Please anyone capable to explain to us if this is normal or this is one alledged reason of this issue ? Thanks

^^ exactly what I was trying to describe. I don't know if it's intended behavior or not. I was in the midst of creating the plunkr last night, but got caught up with other work. It's easy to replicate though. Just enable a form group and pass emitEvent: false, then log the valueChanges and statusChanges of the controls inside the group.
Please provide a solution. This bug along with the disabled attribute not working for reactive forms deadlocked my project
Only workaround I found was to set flag before enabling or disabling any field and checking for it on valueChanges. Quite annoying.
This is a quite annoying bug... Will it be fixed anytime soon?

I actually got it to work by using 
`.enable({ onlySelf: true, emitEvent: false })`
instead of 
`.enable({ emitEvent: false })`

@xavs I don't understand why passing this object signature works , I used your **.disable({ onlySelf: true, emitEvent: false })** in a cross-field validation to dynamically enable/disable a checkbox if another field in the group is invalid. Can someone explain the purpose of the object?
Please fix!!

Up.
Fix will be appreciated.

Got an answer/workaround on SO:
http://stackoverflow.com/questions/43541897/valuechanges-on-formcontrol-triggers-when-form-enable-even-with-emitevent-fals
Just ran in to this problem as well.  The workaround of adding `onlySelf: true` to `.enable` and `.disable` works, but it feels like I shouldn't have to do that.

issue.body:
…is false (#12366)

Previously, the emitEvent flag was only checked when emitting on the current control. Thus, if  the control was part of a hierarchy, events were emitted on the parent and the childrens. This fixes the issue by properly passing the emitEvent flag to both parent and childrens.

Fixes #12366

## What is the current behavior?
<!-- Please describe the current behavior that you are modifying, or link to a relevant issue. -->

See #12366 
For instance, if we have a FormGroup > FormArray > FormControl hierarchy and we disable the FormArray with emitEvent: false, the events (valueChanges, statusChanges) are still emitted on both the FormGroup and the FormControl.

## What is the new behavior?

The emitEvent flag is properly passed to the parent and the childrens. Thus, in our previous example, not events are emitted on neither the FormGroup nor the FormControl
